target_customer: Individuals and families paying for data broker opt-outs, plus businesses protecting employee and executive privacy
problem: Hundreds of data brokers publish and sell home addresses, phone numbers and emails, and manual opt-out is slow and repetitive.
business_model: Consumer and business subscriptions for automated data broker removal, with a free exposure report as the funnel
product_category: Personal data removal and digital footprint management

technical_complexity.rationale: Scraping and automating hundreds of broker opt-out flows with screenshot proof, against changing sites and anti-bot measures, is repetitive but hard to keep reliable.

defensibility.rationale: Broker coverage and removal automation took effort to build but competitors offered similar services; the screenshot proof feature differentiated.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals persisted and grew; Surfshark, which owns Incogni, bought a majority stake in Optery in September 2026 and said Optery would remain standalone.

market_need_then: Privacy law growth and rising doxxing and phishing concern drove demand for broker removal, and reviewers later rated the category as in high demand; no figures dated to 2021 were found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and reassuring consumer privacy voice

branding.brand_signature: Free Exposure Report with live screenshots as proof of exposure and removal
branding.community_and_virality: Faces of Optery profile series; PCMag Editors' Choice awards and wide review coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: Repeated PCMag awards and steady reviewer coverage gave solid category awareness, though competitor Incogni and DeleteMe were more widely known.

outcome_analysis: Optery grew a consumer and business data removal product to a team of about 55, won repeated PCMag Editors' Choice awards and raised only a few million dollars. In September 2026 Surfshark bought a majority stake, keeping Optery standalone next to its Incogni brand. Terms were not disclosed; the capital efficient path ended in a strategic majority sale.
notes: Sources conflict on the lead investor of the 2023 seed (Bayhouse Capital versus Balderton versus Global Founders Capital); investors listed are those named in the company announcement. Unverified later rounds on aggregators (a 4.25M entry dated 2025-04 and a 2.7M entry dated 2025-09); not recorded. Earlier funding before 2023 likely exists (one report cites 6 million total) so coverage is partial. Acquisition is a majority stake, recorded as acquisition because the directory status is Acquired. optery.com timed out when fetched, not confirmed dead. Competitor lists found were 2025 to 2026 comparisons, so none dated near 2021 to 2022; list is empty.
